present_on_scene_date.note: PRESENCE ON THE SCENE DATE IS AN ASSUMPTION OF CONTINUITY AND NOT A STATEMENT. Nothing reached follows this household past 1833. It is graded uncertain rather than present because the town's population roughly quadrupled between the roster and the scene date and a great many of the men on it were, in Andreas's own phrase, 'adventurers, comprising moneyed speculators and prospectors, as yet undecided whether to stay at Chicago or go on'.

occupation.note: 'Ashbel Steele, plastered Calhoun's printing office in November, 1833' - the trade is stated as an act rather than as a title, which is how this roster names several of its artisans.

persons.note: Andreas vol. 1, printed p. 132 (scan p. 281), 'an imperfect list of the denizens of the town in the fall of 1833, not before named'. It gives a name, a trade and usually an arrival year, and it is a retrospective of 1884: a YEAR off it is documented, a MONTH is not, and it says nothing whatever about 1835. THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 2 times: Election returns — poll list of 1834, filed 11 August 1834 — “Steele, Ashbel” (poll_1834_104, line 273); Poll list of 1835 — “Steele, Ashbel” (poll_1835_076, line 363). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Steele' agrees with the entry's forenames; 1 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json). THE FEDERAL TRACT SALES — A TRANSACTION, NOT A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales database records this name entering federal ground around the town: “STEELE ASHBEL” — 3 sales on 1833-10-22, T39N R14E sec 16 (ls0340, ls0341, ls0342). A sale is a TRANSACTION and never a residence — the register's Residence column reads 'UNKNOWN' here, so it says a man of this name was buying land in these years and nothing about where he lived or what stood on the ground. The reading is transcription-mediated; the adjudication is data/research/land_sales/resident_crosswalk.json. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the grade is applied by T-0515 against every source at once, and a purchase corroborates rather than mints.

resident_research.evidence_for: Cook County histories place Ashbel Steele in the early Chicago/Cook County civic record and identify him as county coroner in the 1835 period. This supports continued local presence while stopping short of assigning an unsourced town dwelling.

research_note: THE ONLY PLASTERER IN THE DATASET, AND THE ONLY MAN IN IT DOCUMENTED BY A SINGLE JOB. What makes him worth a record is what the job proves about a building: the town's ordinances of 7 November 1833 legislate for 'wooden buildings with wooden and lath-and-plaster partitions', and this is a named man doing exactly that work in the same month, in a building this dataset models. THE LINK IS NOT MADE IN works_at because plastering a room once is not working somewhere; it is recorded here.

directories.note: LATER EVIDENCE, BESIDE THE 1835 CLAIMS AND NOT INSIDE THEM. A Chicago directory of 1839, 1843 or 1844 meets somebody of this name and this pass records what it prints. Under the ratified ladder a directory read after 1835 can corroborate that a person attested here was still in Chicago and can print a trade or a street the 1835 record never had; on its own it makes nobody a resident of 1835. Nothing on this person's 1835 record was regraded, moved, dated or given an occupation by this entry.
